activate.description: Bring built-in Safari to the foreground through CoreDevice without claiming a rendered page.

open-url.description: Deliver one policy-validated HTTP or HTTPS URL directly through CoreDevice without a separate activation step.

open-url-direct.description: Deliver one caller-supplied HTTP or HTTPS URL directly, with no prelaunch ceremony.

prohibited: delivering any scheme other than HTTP or HTTPS, including x-web-search, x-safari-https, FTP, webclip, or guessed schemes
opening or manipulating private browsing, extension routes, or browser settings
closing, selecting, reordering, grouping, inventorying, or reading any tab outside the explicit request
claiming tab ownership or automatic tab cleanup after URL delivery
submitting forms, downloading files, changing accounts, making payments, performing destructive actions, or handling protected confirmations
replaying URL delivery after dispatch begins or treating CoreDevice acceptance as rendering evidence
safety.uncertain_outcome: Safari may have received the URL, changed history, reused a tab, or created a tab before a response was lost. Inspect with the user and never replay delivery automatically.

device: paired physical iPad with built-in Safari

data_access: one explicit HTTP or HTTPS URL supplied by the caller
data_sent: the explicit URL to Safari and normal browser requests to its destination
privacy.retention: The integration stores no URL or tab inventory. Safari may retain history, website data, and tabs under the user's existing settings; automatic tab cleanup is unsupported.
privacy.notes: Production Safari is CoreDevice-only. Exact-profile route status is held separately in route-compatibility.json: website is proven, while the established YouTube convenience remains public as a candidate for backward compatibility.
